newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids mostly flat despite crude decline.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids mostly flat despite crude decline.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished mostly flat Friday as crude oil prices resumed Wednesday's steep decline on concerns over rising level of imports from foreign suppliers.
NYMEX May crude futures settled down 35 cents at $19.12 a barrel after finishing unchanged yesterday.
High-sulphur materials are still pressurd by aggressive offers, but skepticism is growing that those barrels actually exist due to the lack of buying interest, market sources said.
"It's just people talking. I don't see the barrels," said an East Coast resid trader.
Spot USG three percent prices narrowed to $13.25-50 a barrel from Thursday's $13.25-13.75. USG three percent paper for the rest of April slipped to $12.90-13.15 from $13.10-30 yesterday.
USG one percent physical grade held at $14.75-15.00.
One percent physical, in the New York harbor, remained steady at $15.25-50. One percent NYH paper for balance of April fell to $14.75-95, almost unchanged from Thursday's $14.75-90.
NYH three percent physical widened to $13.25-75 from $13.50-75 Wednesday.

Swing gas deliveries at New York City gate for Monday slipped to $2.07-2.14 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) or $13.23 a barrel equivalent from Thursday's $2.14-2.17/mmBtu or $13.54 a barrel equivalent.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed to $1.90/mmBtu or $11.97/bbl equivalent from $1.87/mmBtu or 11.78/bbl equivalent yesterday.
